Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment budget

Committee of Supply debate on Head L of the Estimates3 March 2026 – 4 March 2026 budget-2905, budget-2907, budget-2913

A Committee of Supply debate on Head L of the Estimates for the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment, covering climate adaptation, water, food, heat, waste and related policies.

The transcript states that from April the Beverage Container Return Scheme will add a 10-cent deposit on marked beverage containers, refundable at reverse vending machines, and that climate vouchers will be expanded next month to include five-tick clothes dryers and induction stoves. It also states that 2026 is designated the Year of Climate Adaptation, that a National Adaptation Plan will be published in 2027, and that portable flood barriers and flood alerts are being made available to residents.

What happens next Ms Poh Li San sought leave to withdraw her amendment; the Coastal Protection Bill will be tabled for Second Reading; the National Adaptation Plan will be published in 2027; the ACT Fund 2 will be available from April 2026; and the SG Eco Fund Climate Adaptation Package starts 1 May 2026.

Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Education budget

Committee of Supply2 March 2026 – 3 March 2026 budget-2896, budget-2902

A Committee of Supply debate on Head K, the Ministry of Education, with Members moving cuts and the Minister and Ministers of State responding.

The debate records changes to primary and secondary education, including the GEP refresh, a single Post-Secondary Admissions Exercise from 2028, Higher Mother Tongue eligibility from Secondary 1, and more financial assistance for lower- to middle-income students from Academic Year 2026. It also records reviews of Primary 1 registration, class sizes, milestone exams and DSA, and a salary review for educators.

Committee of Supply debate on Manpower Ministry budget and labour policies

Committee of Supply3 March 2026 budget-2903

A Committee of Supply debate on Head S (Manpower) of the Estimates, opened by Ms Yeo Wan Ling moving a $100 reduction amendment, with MPs raising labour policy proposals and ministers responding.

The transcript records planned changes including adding eight occupations to the NTS-OL in 2026, raising EP and S Pass qualifying salaries and the Local Qualifying Salary, extending GRIT to the 2026 cohort, and expanding the Overseas Markets Immersion Programme. It also records proposals from MPs on retrenchment benefits, jobseeker support, caregiver leave, and wage thresholds, but does not state that these proposals will be adopted.

Adjournment debate on access to school co-curricular activities

Adjournment motion3 March 2026 matter-adj-2909

An adjournment motion in which Mr Kenneth Tiong spoke on access to co-curricular activities and proposed reforms, followed by a response from Senior Minister of State for Education David Neo, before Parliament adjourned.

The record sets out proposals to widen access to CCAs, including extending the primary school no-trial pilot to secondary schools, allowing students to change CCAs without LEAPS penalty, and expanding cross-school programmes. The Senior Minister of State said MOE and MCCY are working to share facilities and provide professional coaching across schools, that students from lower-income families can tap the MOE Opportunity Fund for CCA expenses, and that strengthening access to CCAs is a key priority. He said more details will be announced at MCCY’s Committee of Supply debates later.

  • The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)

    • The Leader of the House moved that Parliament do now adjourn.

      Verbatim5 words
      That Parliament do now adjourn.

  • Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)

    • Mr Kenneth Tiong said he wished to discuss the co-curricular activities system.

      Verbatim9 words
      I wish to discuss our co-curricular activities (CCA) system.

    • He said each January Secondary 1 students submit a ranked list of CCA preferences.

      Verbatim12 words
      Each January, Secondary 1 students submit a ranked list of CCA preferences.

    • He said schools conduct trials and auditions for popular CCAs, sports and performing arts.

      Verbatim11 words
      For popular CCAs, sports, performing arts, schools conduct trials and auditions.

    • He said students who do not pass are asked to remove that CCA from their choices.

      Verbatim14 words
      Students who do not pass are asked to remove that CCA from their choices.

    • He said CCA is compulsory and students must participate for four to five years.

      Verbatim11 words
      CCA is compulsory. Students must participate for four to five years.

    • He said under LEAPS 2.0 participation is graded and grades translate into bonus points for post-secondary admission.

      Verbatim17 words
      Under LEAPS 2.0, that participation is graded and those grades translate into bonus points for post-secondary admission.

    • He said the Ministry piloted removal of CCA selection trials across eight primary schools in 2020.

      Verbatim15 words
      In 2020, the Ministry piloted the removal of CCA selection trials across eight primary schools.

    • He said about two-thirds of primary schools today operate without trials.

      Verbatim9 words
      Today, about two-thirds of primary schools operate without trials.

    • He proposed extending the primary school pilot to secondary schools.

      Verbatim8 words
      Extend the primary school pilot to secondary schools.

    • He proposed that selection trials sort students into a competitive squad and a developmental programme, not into participants and the excluded.

      Verbatim26 words
      Where a CCA conducts selection trials, these trials should sort students into a competitive squad and a developmental programme – not into participants and the excluded.

    • He proposed every student should be able to join at least one of their top CCA choices.

      Verbatim15 words
      Every student should be able to join at least one of their top CCA choices.

    • He proposed allowing students to change CCAs at the end of Secondary 1 or Secondary 2 without LEAPS penalty.

      Verbatim24 words
      I propose that students be allowed to change CCAs at the end of Secondary 1 or end of Secondary 2 without penalty under LEAPS.

    • He said the SP-CCA programme today serves 232 students from 86 schools across four sports.

      Verbatim16 words
      The Strategic Partnership CCA (SP-CCA) programme today serves 232 students from 86 schools across four sports.

    • He proposed doubling SP-CCA from four sports to eight sports within two years.

      Verbatim13 words
      One, to double SP-CCA from four sports to eight sports within two years.

    • He proposed publishing a sport-by-sport availability map showing which sports are offered at which schools.

      Verbatim23 words
      Two, publish a sport-by-sport availability map, showing which sports are offered at which schools, so that gaps are visible and planning is data-driven.

    • He proposed publishing a five-year SP-CCA expansion roadmap and inviting schools to form voluntary geographic clusters of four to six schools.

      Verbatim30 words
      Three, publish a five-year SP-CCA expansion roadmap with clear targets and invite schools to form voluntary geographic clusters of four to six schools, pooling CCA offerings, so students can cross-attend.

    • He asked whether students in structured external programmes could be eligible for CCA recognition, subject to school verification.

      Verbatim30 words
      Could students participating in a structured external programme – ActiveSG, a National Sports Association, or a registered academy – be eligible for CCA recognition, subject to verification by the school?

    • He asked whether the Junior Sports Academy intake could be doubled or tripled given demand exceeds supply.

      Verbatim30 words
      And at primary level, could we double or triple the Junior Sports Academy intake – this fully Ministry of Education (MOE)-funded, non-competitive, multi-sport programme – given demand already exceeds supply?

    • He proposed CoachSG create a new NROC tier for an Assistant Coach or Recreational Coach credential.

      Verbatim37 words
      I propose that CoachSG create a new NROC tier – an Assistant Coach or Recreational Coach credential, completable in eight to 16 hours at nominal cost, covering maybe Safe Sport, first-aid, values-based coaching and inclusive session design.

    • He proposed reviewing the LEAPS 2.0 Achievement domain.

      Verbatim6 words
      Review the LEAPS 2.0 Achievement domain.

    • He proposed requiring MOE to collect and publish socio-economic data on DSA applications and outcomes.

      Verbatim23 words
      And require MOE to collect and publish socio-economic data on DSA applications and outcomes – household income quartile, participation in paid preparatory programmes.

    • Mr David Neo said the CCA landscape is not perfect and challenges remain.

      Verbatim14 words

    • He said they are working to further widen access for students to a greater diversity of CCAs.

      On access, and selecting one's favourite CCAs, we are working to further widen access for students to a greater diversity of CCAs.

    • He said MOE and MCCY, including Sport Singapore and the National Arts Council, are working together to share facilities and provide professional coaching across schools.

    • He said SP-CCA enables secondary school students to pursue activities beyond what their individual schools offer.

      Verbatim31 words
      I thank the Member for agreeing that we can expand these CCAs to more students and more schools so that students can get to choose and participate in their choice CCA.

    • He said he will announce more details at MCCY’s Committee of Supply debates later.

      Verbatim14 words
      I will announce more details at the MCCY’s Committee of Supply (COS) debates later.

    • He said students from disadvantaged backgrounds will continue to be supported.

      Verbatim12 words
      We will continue to ensure that students from disadvantaged backgrounds are supported.

    • He said students from lower-income families can tap the MOE Opportunity Fund for learning experiences and additional CCA expenses.

    • He said they will explore how to increase access to the Junior Sports Academy programme.

      Verbatim17 words
      And yes, we will explore how to increase access to the Junior Sports Academy programme as well.

    • He said coaches will continue to be required to possess NROC certification.

      Verbatim16 words

      Verbatim31 words
      And as part of this, strengthening access to CCAs for students is a key priority, including allowing more of them their first choice and strengthening access for students from disadvantaged backgrounds.

  • Mr Speaker

    • Parliament adjourned at 9.07 pm.

      Verbatim5 words

What happens next Mr David Neo said he will announce more details at the MCCY’s Committee of Supply debates later; Parliament adjourned at 9.07 pm.

How this page was made

Built from the official Hansard record (Parliament of Singapore Official Reports). No news reporting was used. Briefs are written by software from the transcript and every key point carries the verbatim words it was drawn from.

  • Reports collected: 68 of about 73 (93%)
  • Briefs on this page: 4 (162 verified points)
  • Speaker attribution: 98% of turns carry an explicit speaker tag
  • Any point whose quote could not be found in the transcript was discarded rather than shown.
  • Coverage is below 100%. Some items from this sitting may be missing, so read the totals as a floor rather than a final count.
